title: Can a laundry hanger be printed in two halves on a 220 mm bed, and is the bolted joint strong enough?
summary: A half-lap hub joint with two M4 bolts lets every hanger-fit width up to the 25.8 cm XXL print on a 220 mm bed as one part printed twice. In a beam model with assumed PLA constants, the joint, not the arm, is then the weak point: safety factor 3.7–13 against 40–70 for the arm, set by bolt bearing on the half-depth boss, and the joint needs 4–9 mm of depth against the arm’s 0.8 mm. Printed pegs instead of bolts fail (safety factor 0.9–1.8 for 4 mm pegs). Stylised; nothing was printed or tested.
